repo.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability
repo.name: neovim

body: > Currently there is no reliable way to display virtual line with its own highlighting _till the end of line_. This type of feature is important when virtual lines are used to display diff-style information, like a reference text {i.e. before the change} of the line.(#40994) This PR add a field `virt_lines_eol_hl` to make the **last** `hl` in each `virtlies` **till the end of the** line. For example, you can run lua code: ```lua api.nvim_buf_set_extmark(0, 1, 0, 0, { virt_lines = { { { 'Virtual Line', 'String' }, { '', 'Visual' } } }, virt_lines_eol_hl = true, }) ``` Here is result: When you set `virt_lines_overflow = 'wrap'` use code like: ```lua api.nvim_buf_set_extmark(0, 1, 0, 0, { virt_lines = { { { 'Virtual Line', 'String' }, { string.rep('-', 50), 'Visual' } } }, virt_lines_overflow = 'wrap', virt_lines_eol_hl = true, }) ``` The result is also no problem: In fact, the API design is different from the issue. This is because I think this feature only takes effect at the end, and its behaviors in a single operation are almost same. Therefore, I don’t think it’s necessary to use an complicated design; instead, I simply use a boolean. Of course, this is just my opinion. I’d be happy to improve it then. Actually Close #40994

comment_regular_data.body:
Sorry, I miss a 's' in commit message and cause a check's error. :(
Should I force push to fix it?

This is more of a design question, but I do wonder if it is better to simply always treat a `{ '', 'Group' }` chunk at the end of the virtual line list as a "highlight with this group till the end of line". Right now (if I remember correctly) these chunks are ignored.

Although this might break certain usages, I don't think this would be a (significant) breaking change per se. While at the same time it would allow more flexible behavior (some lines might be highlighted till the end of line while some might not) *and* won't require another extmark option.

> I do wonder if it is better to simply always treat a `{ '', 'Group' }` chunk at the end of the virtual line list as a "highlight with this group till the end of line"

That sounds good. Let's try that here. We can always retreat later if needed.
Ok, I will try it here.

In most cases, this seems to work well. However, when handling empty lines, as the `test` shows, `inline_completion` passes an empty string, leading to unexpected results. Of course, we could add a special exception handle within `inline_completion`. 

But the real concern is whether there’s a large amount of similar code on the user side. We should give this some careful thought.🤔

> In most cases, this seems to work well. However, when handling empty lines, as the `test` shows, `inline_completion` passes an empty string, leading to unexpected results. Of course, we could add a special exception handle within `inline_completion`.
> 
> But the real concern is whether there’s a large amount of similar code on the user side. We should give this some careful thought.🤔

This is probably because it uses a single `{'', 'Group'}` chunk to show an empty virtual line. The same behavior can be achieved by just not supplying any hunks in the future empty virtual line. So instead of `{ { { 'one', 'AAA' } }, { { '', 'BBB' } }, { { 'three', 'CCC' } } }`, using `{ { { 'one', 'AAA' } }, {}, { { 'three', 'CCC' } } }` has the same effect before this PR.

Having to adjust this kind of cases was indeed what I had in mind about ["might break certain usages"](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/41289#issuecomment-5279190441). As having `{ { '', 'BBB' } }` indicate empty virtual line when `{}` works is more complex for no good reason, I think it is reasonable to make them mean two different things as this PR makes it.

The way forward here is probably to also adjust all core usages where there are "dangling" `{ '', 'Group' }` hunks for no good reason.

# Summary of New Work
Here are scenarios where I've found `virt_lines` being used. I'm not familiar with some of these scenarios, so I can't ensure my judgment is entirely accurate.

## fix on new commit
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/2edb1c000958952c87edda596ed9ed53628084ed/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/inline_completion.lua#L249-L256

## other places use `virt_lines`, but no need adjust in my mind
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/2edb1c000958952c87edda596ed9ed53628084ed/runtime/pack/dist/opt/nvim.undotree/lua/undotree.lua#L228

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/2edb1c000958952c87edda596ed9ed53628084ed/runtime/lua/vim/diagnostic/_handlers.lua#L680-L682

## a place I can't quite figure out
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/2edb1c000958952c87edda596ed9ed53628084ed/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/codelens.lua#L224-L234
It seem to add `{'', 'LspCodeLens'}` manuanly, introduced by #38782. To be honest, I don't know if there's a problem with this, or how to adjust it.

> It seem to add `{'', 'LspCodeLens'}` manuanly, introduced by #38782. To be honest, I don't know if there's a problem with this, or how to adjust it.

I am also not quite sure, but it seems it should be safe to use `{}` instead of `{ '', 'LspCodeLens' }`. As this is the same "add an empty line" use case and tests seem to pass with this change.

This is probably not a empty line. It looks like a special trick to prevent flickering by adding an empty text at the end of a line.
